deities: Goddess Iccha Devi (Swayambhu form of Devi; wish-fulfilling goddess)

history.period: Described as 'hundreds of years old' by local listings (verify)
history.summary: Iccha Devi Mandir is a swayambhu (self-manifested) shrine of Goddess Iccha Devi in New Joshi Colony, Tambapura (Navi Peth), Jalgaon. The goddess is regarded as a jagrut (awakened/living) devasthan whose name means 'wish' — devotees believe she fulfills every devotee's wish, hence the name Icchadevi. The shrine sits in a forested, hill-surrounded setting noted by visitors for its quiet atmosphere and hygiene. One local listing calls it 'hundreds of years old', but no documented founding date, builder, or dynasty was found online; treat the antiquity claim as UNVERIFIED. Map services place it at ~20.9947 N, 75.5662 E, near Siddhivinayak and Chetana Hospitals.

town_description: Jalgaon is a major city in northern Maharashtra in the Khandesh region, famous for its banana crop, gold trade, cotton and industries. It is the headquarters of Jalgaon district and a rail and road hub connecting central Maharashtra, with well-known regional pilgrim spots such as Padmalaya and the Manudevi temple nearby. The city sits on the Tapi river plain with the Satpura ranges to the north.
